questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:**

Judicious
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. prudent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Judicious **means *having, showing, or done with good judgement or sense.*

 
• Let's look at the meanings of the given words-

 
 
• **Prudent **means acting with or showing care and thought for the future.

 
 
• **Example - **He always listened to her** prudent** advice.
 
 
 
• ​**Dull **means lacking interest or excitement.
 
 
• Example - They are both nice people but can be rather **dull**. 
 
 
 
• **Foolish** means lacking good sense or judgement; unwise.
 
 
• Example - She's been taking** foolish** risks.
 
 
 
• **Unfair** means not based on or behaving according to the principles of equality and justice.
 
 
• Example - It's **unfair** for them to be allowed to leave early if we can't. 
 
 
 
 

Clearly, 'prudent' is the correct word.

questions.question:
Directions: **Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The meeting will start when the manager__ is arriving.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is a conditional sentence. 'When' puts a condition here.
 
• The sentence says that the meeting will start only after the arrival of the manager.
 
• The structure of the conditional sentence should be** a conditional statement in present tense + simple future ( First conditional)**
 
• Here, **'will'** states that the meeting is scheduled for the future.
 
• So, to make the sentence correct we shall replace the phrase with '**arrives'.**

**Correct sentence**__- *The meeting will start when the manager__ **arrives.**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

 
• Look at the logic and context of the sentence and then focus on choosing the correct tense.

questions.question:
Directions:** ****Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

After the match, every player of the team went back to its house.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02dd327f251548fac247203de325a9c609cc0c19e5f40f0bc250e9ccfde81254.png] 

__
 
• There is an error in the usage of the pronoun **'its'**.
 
• The required pronoun must refer to the player.
 
• So, we must replace '**its**' with 'his/her' to make the sentence correct.

**Correct sentence**__- *After the match, every player of the team went back to his house.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• We use **possessive determiners** before a noun. We use **possessive pronouns** in place of a noun.
 
• In the given sentence we require a possessive determiner before the noun 'house'.
 
• '**Its**' is used to refer to a group, animals, or things.
 
 
• *Eg- The cat hurt its paw.*
 
 
 
• **'His/her'** is used to refer to persons.
 
 
• *Eg- He went back to his house.*

• **Connection** means a relationship in which a person or thing is linked or associated with something else.
 
• **Combination **means a joining or merging of different parts or qualities in which the component elements are individually distinct.
 
• **Connotation** means an idea or feeling which a word invokes for a person in addition to its literal or primary meaning.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, a part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part among the sentences has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click option 4 i.e. 'No error'.

The recently announcement about (A) various government schemes (B)/ impacted the society positively. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02dd327f251548fac247203de325a9c609cc0c19e5f40f0bc250e9ccfde81254.png] 

__
 
• There is an error in **option 1.**
 
• **'Recently' is an adverb** that indicates an action that has been performed not long ago.
 
• In the given sentence, 'announcement' is a noun and we require an adjective that describes the announcement.
 
• **'Recent'** is the adjective form of **'recently**'.

**Correct sentence**__- *The **recent** announcement about various government schemes impacted the society positively.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• ***Adjectives** describe a noun whereas ***adverbs*** describe a verb.*
 
• Adverbs usually have '-ly' as suffix.* Eg- frequently, recently.*
 
• Adjectives usually have suffixes '-ous','-ent','-al','-ive','-less' and '-ful'.* Eg- beautiful, intelligent.*

questions.question:
Directions: **Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Manish has not been attending the class __for last__ month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. since last.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02dd327f251548fac247203de325a9c609cc0c19e5f40f0bc250e9ccfde81254.png] 

__
 
• The given sentence uses** 'has not been attending'** which indicates the sentence is **present perfect continuous tense.**
 
• The **present perfect continuous tense** (also known as the present perfect progressive tense) shows that something started in the past and is continuing at the present time. 
 
• The underlined phrase must be replaced with 'since last' as 'since' is used to indicate that an action started in the past and is still in continuation.

Correct sentence- Manish has not been attending the class **since last month.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] Mistake Points__**

 
• Usually, there is a confusion in the usage of **'for, from and since'**.
 
• The word '**since'** is used to present the starting time of an action that continues in the present till this date.
 
• The word **'from'** is also to present the starting point of an action.
 
• **'For'** is used to indicate a period of time.
 
• So, option 1 is correct.
